strings.name: Annalena Baerbock
strings.role: Former German foreign minister, former president of the 80th UN General Assembly and Columbia professor of professional practice
strings.summary: Baerbock was co-leader of Germany's Greens and the country's first female foreign minister before presiding over the 80th UN General Assembly. She is now a professor of professional practice at Columbia University's School of International and Public Affairs and faculty co-director of its MPA in Global Leadership, focusing on diplomacy, multilateral cooperation and gender equality.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through 18 November 2026. Her Bundestag, foreign-minister and General Assembly posts are historical; Columbia's current faculty page confirms her university roles. The 26 October lecture is supported by an indexed university retrospective, whose full text was not accessible.
strings.influence.rationale: A former German foreign minister engaged in climate and security diplomacy, with public influence in European foreign affairs and UN multilateral affairs.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Earned a political-science Vordiplom at the University of Hamburg and an LL.M. at the London School of Economics in 2005. Her doctoral research was not completed.
strings.facts.f2.label: End of parliamentary service
strings.facts.f2.value: The Bundestag's editorial note records that she submitted her resignation on 15 June 2025 and left parliament at the end of 30 June.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Presenting feminist foreign policy guidelines
strings.highlights.h1.text: Presented guidelines centred on rights, representation and resources in 2023. Advocate Kristina Lunz nevertheless questioned their consistency with military expansion. Policy objectives are distinguished from achieved outcomes.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Convening secretary-general candidate dialogues
strings.highlights.h2.text: As General Assembly president, convened exchanges between candidates, Member States and civil society. The Assembly appoints the Secretary-General on the Security Council's recommendation; its president does not select the officeholder personally.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Hammarskjöld Lecture and medal
strings.timeline.t1.text: An indexed Columbia retrospective reports that she delivered the annual Hammarskjöld Lecture at Uppsala University and received the medal. The full article was not accessible; this retrospective is distinct from earlier event announcements.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Ended her presidency of the 80th General Assembly
strings.timeline.t2.text: An indexed extract of the 81st General Assembly's secretary-general selection page confirms that she conducted the process until this date. She is not described as the current Assembly president thereafter.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Columbia announced her faculty appointment
strings.timeline.t3.text: The school announced that she would become a professor of professional practice and faculty co-director of the MPA in Global Leadership in the autumn. The announcement date is not an asserted first teaching day.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Elected president of the 80th General Assembly
strings.timeline.t4.text: The General Assembly elected her to preside over the session running from September 2025 to September 2026. The election date is distinguished from the session's opening.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became Germany's foreign minister
strings.timeline.t5.text: Succeeded Heiko Maas as Germany's first female foreign minister, serving until May 2025.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Elected co-leader of the Greens
strings.timeline.t6.text: Elected alongside Robert Habeck to lead Alliance 90/The Greens. Her co-leadership continued until 2022.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Entered the German Bundestag
strings.timeline.t7.text: Began serving as a federal MP and was the Greens' parliamentary spokesperson on climate policy from 2013 to 2017.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed her London law master's studies
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed an LL.M. with a public international law focus at the London School of Economics. Her Hamburg Vordiplom and later unfinished doctoral research are recorded separately.
